## magus

This repo is a magus workspace. magus holds a verified model of it: the project
graph, each target's inputs and outputs, and what a diff affects. Ask that model
instead of reading files to rediscover it.

Load the matching magus-* skill (in .claude/skills/, .opencode/skills/ or
.agents/skills/) before you act:

| before you                                                  | load                  |
| ----------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------- |
| git commit, add, stash or reset, or read a diff             | magus-vcs-hygiene     |
| build, test, lint, format or generate                       | magus-run             |
| grep for what exists, depends on or uses X                  | magus-query           |
| answer "how does magus X" from memory                       | magus-upstream-docs   |
| blame magus: a crash, or behavior against its docs          | magus-upstream-source |
| summarize what merged recently                              | magus-change-summary  |
| edit an installed skill, or answer recurring guard feedback | magus-workspace-rules |

Query before grepping.
Routing index: [MAGUS.md](MAGUS.md), what this workspace holds; each project's own MAGUS.md is linked from it.

```sh
magus query "<terms>"        # find and relate entities: kind=spell, project=web, id=~regex
magus explain <node>         # one node: edges, provenance, blast radius
magus refs <symbol>          # where a code symbol is defined and used
```

Run work through targets. A raw `go test`, `eslint` or `pytest` skips the cache,
the sandbox and affected tracking:

```sh
magus run <target> <project> # build, test, lint, format, generate
magus affected ci            # the final gate over everything a diff reaches
```

The guard denies piping or redirecting magus output, and a pipe hides the exit
status. Ask magus for the shape you want:

```sh
magus <cmd> -o name          # ids only
magus <cmd> -o json          # the record; -o template='{{.Field}}' for one field
magus query output <ref>     # a run's full log
```

Before reading a diff or committing, run `magus describe file <path>...`. An
output is generated: regenerate it and commit it with its source, never hand-edit
it.

Prefer the host's magus MCP tools (`client` runs the magus module), and fall back
to the CLI when one is missing or fails. The host manages that connection: never
start a server for it.

Installed magus-* skills are stamped, and `magus agent install --force` erases an
edit. Put workspace-specific instructions in a local magus-local-development
skill beside them.

## This repository

magus builds itself. Learn the layout from the graph (`magus ls`, `magus explain
<path>`, MAGUS.md). This section holds only what no tool says yet; when one starts
saying it, delete it here.

## Binary

- A fresh worktree has no `./magus`, and the guard names the bootstrap. After it,
  run `./magus run install /` for every project's dependencies.
- Never rename `./magus` or move it aside: the hooks and the guard find it by name.

## Conventions

- New generated output goes in a `gen/` dir. A method set is written by hand
  (`types/enums.go`).
- A type a magusfile or script reads lives in `types/`, not behind an alias.
- Language changes in `libs/gopherbuzz/` match upstream Buzz.
- magus is pre-1.0, so breaking is fine: rename, remove or change a name, flag or
  format without a migration path. Add no compat shim, dual reader, fallback for
  older callers or `Deprecated:` alias without asking Eli first.
- Deleting is an option. Before adding code to keep something working, check
  whether removing the old path, flag, fallback, test or doc section reaches the
  goal.
- A shim Eli approved carries `compat(until: <condition>):`. The condition is
  something you can observe ("no store still serves ed25519 envelopes"), never a
  date. Secondary sites say `compat: see <primary site>`. An approved exported API
  gets `// Deprecated:` instead.
- Before proposing a design or reversing one, read what was decided: `magus query
  "kind=docsection id=~decisions/ <terms>"` and the refusal rows in
  [docs/doctrine.md](docs/doctrine.md#a-record-of-refusals). Reopen one only with
  new evidence.
- Merge duplicates only when they share semantics, knobs and bugs; otherwise keep
  the copy with one line saying why
  ([doctrine](docs/doctrine.md#a-copy-can-be-the-right-answer)).
- `TODO`, `FIXME` and `BUG` comments stay; never add `godox` or a linter that
  reports them.
- No silent defaults: a fallback says that it fell back, and an absent capability fails
  loudly rather than answering empty (`docs/doctrine.md`).
- Local state is JSON Lines: one append-only `.jsonl` file per store, one JSON
  object per entry per line. The last line per key wins; compaction is by rename.
  Encoding lives on the entry type (`MarshalJSON`, `UnmarshalJSON`), never in
  a reader that splits lines. Never one rewritten JSON document, TSV or
  `name<TAB>value`
  ([doctrine](docs/doctrine.md#everything-is-a-file)).
- Before fixing behavior that looks wrong, find the test that pins it.
- The docs site is classless Pico: semantic HTML, few custom classes, no inline
  styles.
- A convention that matters gets an enforcement point;
  [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md#where-a-rule-lives) says which. A
  convention kept only in prose holds about half the time.

## Gotchas

- Trust mise once: `mise settings add trusted_config_paths ~/Repos/magus`.
  Untrusted config fails as `govulncheck exited 1` and names neither mise nor trust.
- Args after `--` append to the op's defaults: a package path does not scope a
  run, `-- -run 'TestName'` does. magus flags go before `--`.
- The daemon has no hot reload: after a rebuild, `./magus server stop` then
  `start`. Two builds at one commit share a version, so no skew shows.
